brief: GPT-6 momentum lifted Asian tech and semis, Softbank up approximately 30% in three days. Stronger Japanese wage data reinforces the case for further BOJ tightening, behind a sharp yen appreciation that raises questions about a carry trade unwind hitting global equities and credit, with Japanese exporters underperforming on a stronger currency plus higher energy prices. Energy is the biggest tangible risk to equities: Iran's proposed exclusion zone could constrain ship to ship transfers, Vitol's Hardy puts Hormuz flows at roughly 10m barrels a day with products tight, and Iran says Oman talks are nearing agreement, not yet an operational solution. Copper makes new LME highs, but supply constraints and tariff distortions mean this is not purely a clean growth signal. It fits his view that a spending heavy late cycle economy lets equities and commodities work until energy or rates break demand, so the question is what stops the spending, not whether the Fed hikes. Correcting yesterday, roughly 60bps of hikes is priced through June 2027, not year end, leaving room to price 2.4 to 3 hikes on Thursday PPI and Friday CPI. He reads these as credibility hikes and would lean towards buying a hike driven dip if the AI narrative remains intact.
